gloss: popular song; Japanese popular music (especially Showa era)

definitions.gloss: popular song; Japanese popular music (especially Showa era)
definitions.explanation: A broad category of Japanese popular songs, particularly those from the Showa era (1926-1989). Encompasses various styles including enka and pop ballads that were featured on TV music programs.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}の{歌謡曲|かようきょく}が{好|す}きだ。
カラオケで{歌謡曲|かようきょく}を{歌|うた}うのが{趣味|しゅみ}です。
examples.english: My hobby is singing popular songs at karaoke.

examples.japanese: {昭和|しょうわ}の{歌謡曲|かようきょく}には、{今|いま}でも{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}に{愛|あい}される{名曲|めいきょく}がたくさんある。
examples.english: Among Showa-era popular songs, there are many masterpieces still loved by many people today.

notes:
A culturally important term referring to the mainstream of Japanese popular music, especially from the 1950s through the 1980s. The genre was closely tied to television music shows like NHK's {紅白歌合戦|こうはくうたがっせん}. While the term can technically include all popular songs, it is most strongly associated with the Showa era and is somewhat nostalgic in modern usage.

FORMS:
{歌謡|かよう} (song, ballad) + {曲|きょく} (musical piece)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {昭和|しょうわ}の{歌謡曲|かようきょく}: Showa-era popular songs
- {歌謡曲|かようきょく}{番組|ばんぐみ}: music variety show
- {懐|なつ}かしの{歌謡曲|かようきょく}: nostalgic popular songs
- {歌謡曲|かようきょく}の{名曲|めいきょく}: classic popular songs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- J-POP: Japanese pop music — the modern successor, used from the 1990s onward
- {演歌|えんか}: enka — a specific genre within {歌謡曲|かようきょく}, featuring traditional melodies and emotional vocal style
- {流行歌|りゅうこうか}: popular song — an older term, used more before World War II
